mn51:2.5: The perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas in the future who will lead the mendicant Saṅgha to practice properly at best will do so
mn51:2.6: like the worthy Gotama does in the present.”
mn51:3.4: The perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas in the future who will lead the mendicant Saṅgha to practice properly at best will do so
mn51:3.5: like I do in the present.
mn51:5.13: Sir, I also don’t like the sound of the individual who mortifies others, committed to the practice of mortifying others.
mn51:5.14: Sir, I also don’t like the sound of the individual who mortifies themselves and others, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others.
mn51:5.15: As for the individual who doesn’t mortify either themselves or others, not committed to the practice of mortifying themselves or others, they live without wishes in this very life, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, with self become divine—
mn51:6.9: They neither mortify nor torment themselves or others, both of whom want to be happy and recoil from pain.
mn51:28.5: The Discourse With Kandaraka, the first, is finished.
